summary: xAI launched Voice Agent Builder, a no-code platform in beta for configuring production voice agents on Grok Voice, bundling telephony, knowledge retrieval, tools, guardrails, MCPs and observability, with usage-based pricing.

mechanisms.reason: The product lets voice agents call external APIs, tools and MCP servers to take actions during calls, shifting call-handling work from human seats to autonomous agents.
mechanisms.quote: Knowing the business is only half of a support or sales call. Agents also need to act . They look things up, change records, hand off, or close the loop after the conversation. Tools and connectors are how that happens.

mechanisms.reason: The platform is explicitly positioned to support high-volume production voice-agent traffic, implying more calls and more model inference per deployment.
mechanisms.quote: It’s for operators and developers who want high-volume production voice agents without building the surrounding stack from scratch.

practices.reason: Grok Voice is reported to lead a new voice-agent benchmark under noisy, multi-tool, multilingual call conditions, but the eval is the lab's own and unreplicated.
practices.quote: We trained Grok Voice on those calls. τ -voice Bench measures agents under the same conditions.

practices.reason: The document describes a concrete, implementable agent-building pattern (prompt plus knowledge base plus tools plus guardrails on a single speech-to-speech path) with a stated setup time of about two minutes.
practices.quote: Setup is simple: write a plain-language description of how calls should flow, then attach your documents, tools, and guardrails. You can go from zero to a working agent in about two minutes.

practices.reason: τ-voice Bench introduces a measurement approach for voice agents under realistic call conditions (noise, accents, interruptions, many languages) that changes what teams should test for, though it is the lab's own leaderboard.
practices.quote: Real calls come with low-quality telephony audio, background noise, strong accents, interruptions, and callers who change their minds mid-sentence.

practices.reason: The stated per-minute billing structure and SIP/WebSocket connectivity options are concrete integration terms a team would need to plan for before adopting the product.
practices.quote: Agents are billed at our API rate (currently $0.05 / min of audio ), with voices included and no separate platform fee. Telephony on a free provisioned number is an additional $0.01 / min .
